strings.title: Poisoned Honey
strings.hint: Honey from a single apiary… why did only one customer die? Look for the jar bearing a different number.
strings.solvedText:
The culprit: apiary partner Saber Wannas.

The victim, the apiary's principal owner, had decided to end their partnership and dismiss Saber after discovering his manipulation of the accounts. Saber planned to kill him and implicate him in a "mass food poisoning" scandal that would destroy the apiary's reputation. He injected one jar of honey with plant poison and sent it to the victim as a personal gift from a fictitious customer, intending to make it look like a contaminated batch. But the other jars were safe, exposing a targeted attack rather than mass contamination.

The lethal jar's batch number matching no real batch, the same poison in Saber's shed, and the falsified accounts the victim was about to expose proved his guilt.
strings.summary.text: Hamdan Tawfiq, owner of the region's most famous apiary, died of poisoning after eating a spoonful of his own honey. Panic spread: was the entire batch contaminated? But tests on dozens of jars from the same batch came back completely clear. Only one jar contained poison, the one delivered to the victim as a gift from a customer who did not exist.
strings.summary.victim.name: Hamdan Tawfiq
strings.summary.timeline[0].l: A gift jar arrives in a customer's name
strings.summary.timeline[1].l: The victim tastes honey from the jar in the morning
strings.scene.address: Al-Wadi Apiary — the storeroom and administration office
strings.scene.intro: Shelves full of identical honey jars bearing a single batch number. Only the lethal jar bears a number that matches no batch in the records. It arrived wrapped as a personal gift from an unregistered customer.
strings.scene.photos[0].cap: The honey storeroom and jar shelves
strings.scene.notes[0]: One poisoned jar among dozens of safe ones
strings.scene.notes[1]: The lethal jar's batch number is absent from the records
strings.scene.notes[2]: It arrived as a gift from a fictitious customer
strings.scene.notes[3]: The poison is an extract of a local plant
strings.evidence[0].title: The Lethal Jar
strings.evidence[0].desc: Honey mixed with plant poison. Its printed batch number matches no real batch in the records.
strings.evidence[1].title: Gift Card
strings.evidence[1].desc: Signed by a "loyal customer" who does not exist in the customer database. The handwriting matches the partner's.
strings.evidence[2].title: Poison in the Shed
strings.evidence[2].desc: An extract of the same poisonous plant in a container in the partner's shed. It has no legitimate use in beekeeping.
strings.evidence[3].title: Falsified Accounts
strings.evidence[3].desc: Manipulation of apiary profits in the partner's favor over two years, which the victim was about to expose.
strings.evidence[4].title: Draft Partnership Termination
strings.evidence[4].desc: A decision to dismiss the partner and end the partnership, dated three days before the death.
strings.suspects[0].name: Saber Wannas
strings.suspects[0].alibi: "I was at the market selling honey all morning."
strings.suspects[0].statement: Hamdan was my brother and partner for ten years. We built this apiary from a single hive. The accounts were minor disagreements we would have resolved. Whoever poisons our honey destroys my livelihood too. Look for a competitor who envies our reputation, not a partner who lives by it.
strings.suspects[1].name: Fawzi, the Business Rival
strings.suspects[1].alibi: "I was at an agricultural exhibition in another city. There are photographs."
strings.suspects[1].statement: We compete through quality, not poison. A reputation for contaminated honey hurts me too, because people will fear all the region's honey. My attendance at the exhibition is recorded and photographed throughout the day.
strings.suspects[2].name: Jaber, the Seasonal Worker
strings.suspects[2].alibi: "I was filling jars on the line in front of the other workers."
strings.suspects[2].statement: I fill honey jars as the bosses instruct. I know nothing of their accounts or disputes. All the jars I fill have the same number on the screen. Whoever printed a different number did it off the packing line. It wasn't me.
strings.witnesses[0].name: Victim's wife
strings.witnesses[0].statement: The jar arrived carefully wrapped, in the name of a customer thanking him for the honey. Hamdan was delighted and said: "A loyal customer deserves for me to taste his gift first." We didn't know anyone by that name.
strings.witnesses[1].name: Apiary Accountant
strings.witnesses[1].statement: A few days ago, Hamdan asked me for two full years of statements. He said he suspected his partner of stealing from him. He was quietly angry, the most dangerous kind of anger for him.
strings.witnesses[2].name: Storeroom Worker
strings.witnesses[2].statement: Every batch has one number printed on the line. I once saw Saber using the printer alone after hours. He said he was replacing a damaged label.
strings.folders[0].name: Incident reports
strings.folders[0].docs[0].title: Poisoning Report
strings.folders[0].docs[0].body: The apiary owner's death by poisoning was reported. All honey batches were immediately seized for fear of contamination.
strings.folders[1].name: Forensic medicine
strings.folders[1].docs[0].title: Toxicology report
strings.folders[1].docs[0].body: A lethal dose of poisonous plant extract mixed into honey, present in only one jar.
strings.folders[1].docs[1].title: Batch Examination
strings.folders[1].docs[1].body: All the batch's jars are completely safe. The contamination was a deliberate individual attack, not an accidental mass incident.
strings.folders[2].name: Forensic evidence
strings.folders[2].docs[0].title: Batch Number Examination
strings.folders[2].docs[0].body: The lethal jar's number does not appear in production records. It was printed separately on the apiary's machine after hours.
strings.folders[2].docs[1].title: Gift Card Handwriting Comparison
strings.folders[2].docs[1].body: The gift card's handwriting closely matches partner Saber Wannas's writing.
strings.folders[3].name: Interviews
strings.folders[3].docs[0].title: Saber Interview
strings.folders[3].docs[0].body: He could not explain the false number or his use of the printer after hours. He evaded questions about the accounts.
strings.folders[3].docs[1].title: Rival Interview
strings.folders[3].docs[1].body: Photographs document his presence at the exhibition throughout the day.
strings.folders[3].docs[2].title: Worker Interview
strings.folders[3].docs[2].body: Other workers confirm his position on the packing line.
strings.folders[4].name: Confidential files
strings.folders[4].docs[0].title: Poison Match Report
strings.folders[4].docs[0].body: The poison in Saber's shed exactly matches the lethal jar's poison in composition and origin.
strings.folders[4].docs[1].title: Confession Record
strings.folders[4].docs[1].body: Confronted with the false number, poison, and handwriting, Saber broke down: "He was going to throw me out and take everything I built with him."
strings.reports[0].title: Individual Targeting Report
strings.reports[0].author: Investigation team
strings.reports[0].body: A safe batch plus one poisoned jar bearing a false number, delivered as a gift, means a personal attack disguised as mass contamination.
strings.reports[1].title: Motive Report
strings.reports[1].author: Assigned investigator
strings.reports[1].body: The imminent end of the partnership and exposure of financial fraud provide a direct motive for the partner alone.
strings.notes[0].text: A safe batch and one lethal jar = an individual target
strings.notes[1].text: A batch number absent from the records = secretly printed
